project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence:
Root-cause sink: core/src/main/java/io/undertow/server/handlers/resource/FileResourceManager.java, method getResource(String p), specifically line 89 `File file = new File(base, path);` and line 90 `return new FileResource(file, this, path);` (inside the `if (file.exists())` block starting line 90-96 in the current source). The trust boundary crossed is: caller-supplied relative resource path (attacker-controlled via HTTP request path / servlet path-info / ServletContext.getRealPath argument) -> filesystem File resolution with no verification that the resolved canonical path is still contained within the configured `base` directory. The only existing check (`file.getCanonicalFile().getName().equals(file.getName())`) only compares the last path segment for case-sensitivity and provides zero containment guarantee.

Verified live: reverting to the original code and re-running the harness in the Docker container reproduces the escape (exit 0); adding a canonical-path containment check at the same location (temporarily, then reverted) makes the harness report SAFE and exit 1 — confirming the POV is tied to the actual defect, not a simulated check.

Every distinct source-to-sink path in the alert converges on this one sink, so a complete fix must guard all of them:
1. Trace 1 (direct): any caller of FileResourceManager.getResource(String) with an unnormalized path — e.g. core ResourceHandler passing exchange.getRelativePath() when no CanonicalPathHandler is installed in the pipeline.
2. Trace 2: servlet/src/main/java/io/undertow/servlet/spec/ServletContextImpl.java:313/316 getRealPath(path) -> CanonicalPathUtils.canonicalize(path) (core/src/main/java/io/undertow/util/CanonicalPathUtils.java, canonicalize()/realCanonicalize()) -> FileResourceManager.getResource(canonicalPath). CanonicalPathUtils only recognizes '/' as a segment separator (see the switch on `case '/':` in canonicalize()), so any ".." segment delimited by a backslash is left completely untouched by the "canonicalization" — on Windows, java.io.File then treats '\\' as a live separator and the untouched ".." escapes the base, even though the caller believes the path was already sanitized.
3. Trace 3: servlet/src/main/java/io/undertow/servlet/handlers/DefaultServlet.java:129 getPath(req) reading RequestDispatcher.INCLUDE_PATH_INFO/INCLUDE_SERVLET_PATH attributes (settable by including/forwarding servlets or filters) at line 134 `resourceManager.getResource(path)` — no canonicalization call at all before the sink.
4. Trace 4: same DefaultServlet.getPath(req)/doGet path but via request.getPathInfo()/getServletPath() (raw, attacker-controlled URL path) at line 134 — again no canonicalization before the sink.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: FileResourceManager.getResource("/../secret.txt") (called against a manager whose base is a temp "webroot" directory) resolves and returns a non-null FileResource whose canonical file path equals a sensitive file located in the PARENT of webroot (i.e. outside the configured resource root). The harness prints "VULNERABLE: ..." and exits 0. After a correct fix, getResource() must refuse to return a Resource whose canonical path escapes base, so the harness prints "SAFE: ..." and exits 1.
parsed_output.notes: POV targets alert trace 1 (the direct FileResourceManager.getResource sink) because all four traces in the alert terminate at the identical lines (FileResourceManager.java 80/89/90) — it is the true shared root cause, and exercising it directly gives a deterministic, OS-independent reproduction that works inside the Linux build container (the Windows-specific backslash bypass described in traces 2-4 cannot be observed as an actual filesystem escape on a Linux JVM, since java.io.File only treats '\\' as a separator on Windows). The POV instead uses the OS-agnostic ".." traversal, which reveals that FileResourceManager.getResource() performs NO containment check at all (only a last-segment case-sensitivity check), so it is vulnerable on every platform, with the Windows backslash issue in CanonicalPathUtils/ServletContextImpl/DefaultServlet as an additional, alert-documented way to smuggle unnormalized ".." sequences into this same sink. I validated the POV is genuinely tied to the defect (not a fake check) by temporarily adding a canonical-path containment guard at the sink and confirming the harness flips from exit 0 (VULNERABLE) to exit 1 (SAFE), then reverted that temporary edit — no product code changes remain; only files under .security-pipeline/pov/ were added.
parsed_output.regression_hint:
Invariant a correct fix must enforce: for every path handed to FileResourceManager.getResource(String p) (and any equivalent resource-manager implementation), the File resolved from `base` + the caller-supplied relative path must have a canonical path that is exactly `base` or starts with `base + File.separator`; any resolution that escapes must return null (or throw) before a Resource/FileResource is constructed. This check must happen at (or immediately after) FileResourceManager.java's `new File(base, path)` call (currently ~line 89), not only earlier "canonicalization" of the incoming string, since:
 - CanonicalPathUtils.canonicalize() must also normalize/reject backslash ('\\') as a path-separator-equivalent on all platforms (not just rely on OS-specific File separator behavior), otherwise Windows deployments remain exploitable even when callers "pre-canonicalize" via ServletContextImpl.getRealPath.
 - DefaultServlet.doGet's getPath(req) path (both the INCLUDE_* attribute variant and the plain getPathInfo()/getServletPath() variant) must not be allowed to reach FileResourceManager.getResource without going through the same containment check, since it currently performs zero canonicalization before calling the resource manager.

Known bypass variants the fix must also block (test each, not just the plain "/../" case exercised by this POV):
 - Plain forward-slash traversal: "/../secret.txt", "/a/../../secret.txt" (exercised here — must remain blocked).
 - Backslash-delimited traversal on Windows: "..\\..\\secret.txt", "/a\\..\\..\\secret.txt" (bypasses CanonicalPathUtils since it only special-cases '/').
 - Mixed separators: "/a/..\\../secret.txt".
 - URL-encoded / double-encoded dot-segments arriving through the servlet path-info or dispatcher INCLUDE_PATH_INFO/INCLUDE_SERVLET_PATH request attributes (trace 3), since those bypass normal URL decoding/normalization performed earlier in the pipeline.
 - Absolute-path style payloads on Windows such as "C:\\..\\secret.txt" or UNC paths ("\\\\host\\share\\...") that java.io.File may honor as absolute, bypassing the `base` prefix entirely regardless of ".." handling.
 - Paths that exist under `base` as a symlink pointing outside `base` (not exercised by this POV, but relevant if the fix relies solely on lexical ".." stripping rather than actual canonical-path containment).
parsed_output.summary: Created a real POV that calls the unmodified io.undertow.server.handlers.resource.FileResourceManager#getResource(String) API with a "/../secret.txt" traversal payload and shows it returns a Resource pointing at a file outside the configured base/web-root directory. This is the single shared sink for all 4 traces in the alert (FileResourceManager.java lines 80/89/90), reachable both directly and via ServletContextImpl#getRealPath (CanonicalPathUtils.canonicalize) and DefaultServlet#doGet (getPath(req)).

parsed_output.patch_notes: Added a private isChildOfBase(File) helper in FileResourceManager that compares file.getCanonicalPath() against new File(base).getCanonicalPath() (exact match or proper descendant via File.separator prefix), called right after `new File(base, path)` / `file.exists()` and before the existing case-sensitivity check and FileResource construction. Any resolution that escapes `base` now returns null instead of a Resource. Added FileResourceManagerTestCase (plain JUnit, no server harness needed) verifying: (1) a normal in-base resource is still served, (2) forward-slash traversal variants ("/../secret.txt", "/a/../../secret.txt", "../secret.txt") are blocked, (3) backslash-delimited traversal variants are blocked (meaningfully exercised on Windows; on Linux they degrade to a nonexistent single-segment filename, which is already null, so the test still documents/enforces the invariant cross-platform). Verified against the provided POV harness: before the fix it printed VULNERABLE (exit 0); after the fix it prints "SAFE: getResource(\"/../secret.txt\") returned null (traversal blocked)" (exit 1). Full `mvn -B -DskipTests package` build succeeds across all modules (core, servlet, examples, websockets-jsr).
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk: the added check only rejects resolutions whose canonical path falls outside the configured base directory — legitimate in-base requests (including symlinks that resolve to a location still under base) are unaffected, confirmed by existing FileHandlerTestCase/FileHandlerIndexTestCase passing unchanged. One behavior change to be aware of: if `base` itself is configured as (or contains) a symlink whose target is intentionally outside the nominal base path, and callers rely on serving through that symlink to an external directory, this fix would now block those requests, since containment is computed against base's own canonical path. This matches the security intent of the alert (no silent escape from the configured resource root) and is the standard mitigation pattern for this CWE class. No dependency or API surface changes; only internal behavior of FileResourceManager.getResource tightened.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal at the shared root cause: FileResourceManager.getResource(String) resolved `new File(base, path)` and returned a FileResource with no check that the resolved file actually stayed within `base` — only a last-path-segment case check existed. Added a canonical-path containment check (isChildOfBase) immediately after file resolution: the resolved file's canonical path must equal the canonical base directory or be a descendant of it (via File.separator-based prefix match), otherwise getResource returns null before any Resource is constructed. Since all four alert traces (direct ResourceHandler calls, ServletContextImpl.getRealPath, and both DefaultServlet.getPath variants) converge on this exact sink, the fix blocks every path in the alert without needing to patch each caller individually. Because the check relies on java.io.File's own platform-correct canonicalization/separator handling, it also closes the Windows-specific backslash bypass path (CanonicalPathUtils only handling '/') without needing changes to CanonicalPathUtils itself — the sink now refuses escapes regardless of what separator smuggled the ".." through.

parsed_output.diff_review: Reviewed patch_only.diff, pov.diff, and full.diff (file set matches across all three; content identical, only diff ordering differs — confirmed via diff of concatenation vs full.diff, no unexpected files). Product change is confined to core/src/main/java/io/undertow/server/handlers/resource/FileResourceManager.java: adds a private isChildOfBase(File) helper comparing file.getCanonicalPath() against new File(base).getCanonicalPath() (exact match or proper descendant via File.separator-prefixed startsWith), invoked right after file.exists() and before the pre-existing case-sensitivity check and FileResource construction. This is a standard, minimal, correct mitigation pattern for CWE-022: it checks the fully resolved canonical path rather than lexically stripping ".." tokens, so it is agnostic to '/' vs '\\' delimiters and closes the traversal regardless of how the ".." segments were smuggled in (matches the regression_hint's requirement that containment be enforced at the sink, not just via upstream string canonicalization). The only other product-adjacent change is a new test file (FileResourceManagerTestCase.java) exercising in-base access (must still succeed) and forward-slash/backslash traversal payloads (must be blocked) — appropriate regression coverage, not test-only masking of the vulnerability. No changes to CanonicalPathUtils, DefaultServlet, or ServletContextImpl were made, but since all four alert traces converge on this exact FileResourceManager sink, guarding it here blocks every path in the alert without needing per-caller patches — a reasonable and sufficient fix scope. No unrelated or overly broad changes were introduced. Files under .security-pipeline/pov/ (PovPathTraversal.java, run_pov.sh) are POV harness files only, untouched by the patch commit itself, and the PoV logic (payload "/../secret.txt", VULNERABLE/SAFE + exit code semantics) is unmodified and unweakened.

parsed_output.summary: The patch adds a canonical-path containment check (isChildOfBase) in FileResourceManager.getResource(String) immediately after resolving `new File(base, path)` and before constructing/returning a FileResource. If the resolved file's canonical path is not equal to, or a descendant of, the canonical base directory, getResource now returns null instead of a Resource. This directly closes the shared sink identified in all four alert traces (FileResourceManager.java lines 89-90). The change is minimal, self-contained, and does not alter or weaken the POV. A new regression test (FileResourceManagerTestCase) covers normal in-base access plus forward-slash and backslash traversal variants. Independently rebuilt and reran the POV and the specified regression test suite inside the Docker container; results match the orchestrator's reported logs exactly.
